# SEC-005: Private keys are readable by their owner only

- **Group:** Secrets on disk
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

SSH private keys (~/.ssh/id_* without .pub), *.key and *.pem files under /root and /home give whoever reads them the identity they hold. OpenSSH refuses keys readable by others, but other programs do not, and a readable key is as good as a stolen one. A .pem may also be a public certificate; stackward cannot tell because it never reads contents.

## Verify by hand

```sh
find /root /home -maxdepth 4 \( -name 'id_*' ! -name '*.pub' -o -name '*.key' -o -name '*.pem' \) -perm /077 -ls
```

## How to fix it

chmod 600 the key files (and 700 their folder).

Run `stackward explain SEC-005` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
